title: Brian Fox and the Creation of Bash (1989)
explainer: Bash wasn't the original Unix shell — it was written in 1989 by Brian Fox, an employee of the Free Software Foundation, specifically as a free replacement for AT&T's proprietary Bourne shell, so a fully free GNU operating system wouldn't need any licensed Unix code. Its name, 'Bourne-Again Shell,' is a pun on both the shell it replaced and the FSF's free-software mission. Every habit this module drills — `[ ]` tests, `$(...)`, `set -euo pipefail` — is specific to that 1989 program, not some generic 'the shell.'
